title: Semantic drift in shadow + A/B rollout — postmortem and soft-stop automation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: During a staged rollout that combined shadow traffic (30%) and an A/B canary (15%) for the new embedding variant v3-quant, we observed a coherent semantic drift in downstream reranking and search relevance. The symptom set included: sudden drop in top-5 relevancy for a subset of queries, higher user-visible rerank churn, and an increase in ’user-corrected’ indicator events in the session logs. The incident occurred in staging but was reproducible in a small subset of production traffic replay. The rollout was paused manually after detection but revealed gaps in telemetry and in the auto-rollback policy that prevented an automatic safehold. This ticket collects the postmortem, immediate mitigations, runbook changes, and implementation work for a new "soft-stop" automation that prevents partial promotions from causing prolonged degradation.

root_cause: A confluence of three issues: (1) quantization changes in v3-quant altered the embedding vector normalization distribution (small but systematic), (2) an unrelated runtime change to KV cache key derivation (hash salt ordering) caused mismatched prefixing between offline precompute and runtime cache lookups, and (3) the auto-rollback policy only evaluated token-level error/scoring deltas and did not include embedding-similarity or rerank-quality metrics. Together these caused the canary to return semantically shifted embeddings and occasional stale KV cache hits, producing lower rerank quality and confusing the detection heuristics.
mitigations: Immediate: pause canary promotion, revert A/B traffic to stable model variant
Immediate: purge KV caches on canary pods and run consistency checks across cache namespaces
Hotfix: unify embedding normalization code path between offline precompute and runtime (small patch merged and deployed to staging)
Short-term: add an embedding-similarity metric to the streaming evals and to the rollback policy (threshold + hysteresis)
Short-term: add a pre-rollout invariant check that verifies cache-key derivation matches offline keys for a sampled set of prefixes
Medium-term: implement 'soft-stop' automation that pauses promotions and holds canary traffic while running a fast, targeted regression battery
runbook_updates: Add a new section 'embedding drift' with detection checklist (top-k semantic drop, embedding L2/ cosine shift, and rerank KPI delta)
Document exact console commands to purge KV caches and to force segment-level cache invalidation
Add play for 'soft-stop' invocation: aggressive snapshotting of recent traffic + hold routing + escalation to SRE and ML lead
Include scripted verification steps: run replay on last 2 hours of traffic, compute baseline vs candidate embedding distances, run a small rerank quality A/B test (50k queries)
Update auto-rollback runbook: include embedding-based alarms and tie rollback to 'semantic regression' composite metric

notes: This incident highlights how small numerical shifts from quantization can cascade into product-visible regressions when combined with subtle runtime changes (cache key hashing).
Longer term we should add a model-level contract for embedding invariants (normalization, dtype, key derivation) and enforce them at the model onboarding gate.
Soft-stop is intentionally conservative: it should buy time for deterministic checks (replay, cache validation, unit tests) rather than immediately rolling back and risking flapping.
